title: Local Law 18: transaction verification makes existing STR limits enforceable
dates: Enacted 2022-01-09; platform enforcement 2023-09-05; FY26 update available
rule: Platforms must verify registration before processing covered bookings. Residential stays under 30 days generally require a permanent occupant present and no more than two paying guests. Rent-regulated and NYCHA units cannot register.
observed_evidence: Airbnb disclosed NYC represented approximately 1% of global revenue before enforcement. OSE reports over 3,500 active approved hosts in FY26; these are registrations, not Airbnb listing counts.
abnb_implication: Best documented case for how a city can restrict Airbnb's bookable supply through the payment/booking platform. Lost local nights may partly migrate to nearby destinations, longer stays or hotels sold by Airbnb.
limitations: The 1% is historical gross exposure, not a measured 1% consolidated revenue loss. LL18 enforces longstanding housing rules; compliant home-sharing remains legal. City housing-benefit claims and Airbnb's claims about hotel prices are not causal estimates.
next_catalyst: Registration renewals expected October 2026; enforcement and any enacted amendments.

title: Listing removals and EUR64.1m Airbnb fine
status: Implemented enforcement; fine disputed; May 2026 surety bond suspends enforcement pending court proceedings
dates: Removal order 2025-05-19; removals July 2025; fine December 2025; stay denied March 2026
rule: Consumer authorities pursued missing/incorrect regional licence identifiers, misleading host identity information and failures to comply with information/removal orders.
observed_evidence: Ministry reported 65,122 offending advertisements removed by July 2025. The December 2025 fine was EUR64,055,311. A March 2026 request to stay payment was denied, but the Q2 2026 Form 10-Q subsequently discloses a EUR70m ($80m) surety bond obtained in May 2026 to suspend enforcement pending resolution. Airbnb describes the fine at approximately EUR65m ($76m) and the potential loss as neither probable nor estimable.
abnb_implication: Direct platform liability plus reduced bookable inventory makes this the clearest national enforcement case. Cash/legal expense and recurring supply risk require separate model lines.
limitations: Ads are not necessarily unique productive properties. Removal orders overlap. Bond face value is not a recognized expense or proof of equal cash payment; bond premium/collateral not quantified here. Do not assume the consumer fine is automatically excluded from adjusted EBITDA.
next_catalyst: Court resolution, bond conditions, and changes in accounting recognition or cash settlement.

title: 2025 national registration rollout; 2026 partial annulment
dates: Operational rollout 2025-07-01; judgment 2026-05-19, published 2026-06-08; consolidated law updated 2026-07-18
rule: RD1312/2024 introduced a national registration procedure and digital data gateway. The Supreme Court annulled the single-registry procedure and property/movable-register inscription requirement, including Articles 5 and 8-10 and related provisions.
observed_evidence: The official consolidated BOE text explicitly records annulment; this changes the status of widely reported 2025 registration requirements.
abnb_implication: Historical delistings still matter, but continuing national-register supply haircuts cannot be based on the original decree alone. Regional licensing and surviving EU reporting obligations remain distinct.
limitations: Current replacement/implementation mechanics need further confirmation before host-level modeling. The judgment does not establish that all regional STR rules or the consumer fine were cancelled.
next_catalyst: Replacement legislation, platform implementation notices, and any reactivation of listings.

title: Freeze on first registrations; transfer-related loss of eligibility
dates: 2025-01-01 through 2026-12-31; Law 5313/2026 adds current transfer treatment
rule: New first registrations are prohibited in specified central districts. Current government guidance says covered properties transferred during life are removed from the registry and cannot re-register while the restriction lasts.
observed_evidence: Government housing portal confirms the 2026 extension and transfer restriction; minimum first-offence fine EUR20,000.
abnb_implication: Restricts new supply and can erode incumbent supply as ownership changes. This is more consequential than a purely grandfathered new-entry freeze.
limitations: No company-disclosed city revenue loss identified. Not an Athens-wide or Greece-wide ban on existing compliant STRs.
next_catalyst: Year-end extension, enforcement against transfer/re-registration workarounds.

title: Athens-style freeze expands to a second city
rule: First-time STR registrations suspended in the first municipal community, with the government's transfer restriction applying to the covered areas.
observed_evidence: Official housing portal confirms start/end dates and geographic boundary.
abnb_implication: Provides evidence of domestic replication of a housing-driven restriction. Constrains future destination capacity and legal listing replacement.
limitations: Does not eliminate all Thessaloniki supply. No quantified ABNB financial impact identified.
next_catalyst: Extension beyond December 2026 and expansion to other districts.

title: Revised AL containment zones
rule: Absolute containment applies at ratios of at least 10% AL establishments to permanent housing at municipal/parish/neighbourhood levels; relative containment at 5% to below 10%. New permissions and transfers are constrained, subject to exceptions.
observed_evidence: Final published regulation confirms thresholds; earlier proposal used different thresholds. The final text controls. Follow-up: city reported cancellation of 6,765 registrations described as inactive because required insurance evidence was missing. This is a separate compliance-cleanup cohort, not 6,765 demonstrated productive Airbnb removals.
abnb_implication: Limits growth in saturated neighbourhoods even after national liberalisation. Transfer restrictions and limited exceptions affect replacement supply and host property values.
limitations: Ratios use regulatory establishments and census housing, not Airbnb active listings. Do not assume a citywide removal of all existing AL or use an earlier temporary suspension as the current rule.
next_catalyst: Monthly ratio monitoring, containment maps, exceptions and licence transfers.

title: Mais Habitacao restrictions partly reversed
rule: The 2023 package curtailed new AL registrations with territorial exceptions and added renewal/administrative restrictions. The 2024 decree repealed housing measures and returned stronger discretion to municipalities.
observed_evidence: Official original package and later decree document a change in national policy direction.
abnb_implication: Useful counterweight to a one-way regulatory bear case: national restrictions can reverse while municipal constraints persist. Model Lisbon separately from rural Portugal.
limitations: Do not present the 2023 national registration freeze or automatic renewal regime as unchanged current law. Separate tax repeal details require their own law; not modeled here.
next_catalyst: Municipal containment decisions and national changes to the decentralised framework.

title: Principal-residence cap reduced from 120 to 90 days
rule: Main residences may be rented as tourist furnished accommodation for 90 days per year instead of 120, subject to legal exceptions. Other premises face separate authorisation rules.
observed_evidence: City guidance confirms implementation and ongoing 90-day limit.
abnb_implication: Reduces annual sellable nights of hosts who previously rented above 90 days; can particularly constrain peak-demand capacity and increase compliance friction.
limitations: A 25% reduction in the legal ceiling is not a 25% reduction in Paris nights or ABNB revenue. Many hosts operate below the cap; professional licensed accommodation follows different rules.
next_catalyst: Enforcement and separate proposals targeting multi-property operators.

title: 15-night cap in eight central neighbourhoods
rule: Selected Centre and De Pijp neighbourhoods moved from 30 to 15 holiday-rental nights annually. Nights already rented before April count toward 2026's cap.
observed_evidence: Current Dutch city guidance lists eight covered areas and directs hosts to adjust incompatible reservations. Older English page describes a proposal and is stale on status.
abnb_implication: Restricts capacity of occasional whole-home hosts in highly visited neighbourhoods and demonstrates further tightening after earlier regulation.
limitations: Not a citywide 15-night rule; not all B&B/hotel supply is covered. Halving the cap does not establish a halving of actual bookings.
next_catalyst: Compliance, cancellations and any further geographic expansion.

title: Principal-residence requirement and platform registry verification
rule: Covered communities limit STRs to a principal residence plus one secondary suite or accessory dwelling unit. Provincial registration and platform duties extend beyond the residence-rule geography, with exemptions.
observed_evidence: January 2025 government statement described an approximately 10% decline in entire-home listings from March 2024. A newer June 2, 2026 government release reports active STR listings declining from 28,000 to just over 23,000. These are different metric/time references and neither isolates a causal Airbnb revenue loss.
abnb_implication: Large subnational example of housing policy restricting investment-property supply and requiring platform participation.
limitations: Government-reported listing change is not a causal estimate or ABNB-specific revenue result. Resort/exempt properties and local opt-in/out rules require address-level classification.
next_catalyst: Registry enforcement, geographic exemptions and annual opt-in/out changes.

title: Seasonal restriction on principal-residence tourist rentals
rule: In most boroughs, principal residences may host tourist rentals only June 10 through September 10. Commercial tourist homes face separate zoning and permit restrictions.
observed_evidence: City guidance confirms seasonality and borough variation.
abnb_implication: Restricts off-season capacity and raises compliance burden; lawful commercial inventory may partly offset the loss.
limitations: Not a blanket ban on all Montreal Airbnb listings; commercial rules vary by borough. No ABNB-specific dollar loss established.
next_catalyst: 2026 autumn enforcement; legal commercial supply and borough changes.

title: Plan RESIDE and enforcement against illegal tourist flats
rule: City protects residential use and shifts tourist accommodation away from dispersed flats in residential buildings in the historic centre; compliant accommodation categories remain possible.
observed_evidence: City's 2025 implementation report confirms September commencement. Q3 2025 Airbnb call names Madrid as a regulation-constrained hotel-pilot market.
abnb_implication: Directly connects policy constraints with Airbnb's hotel strategy. Growth may require a different accommodation mix rather than simple host acquisition.
limitations: Grandfathering, building use and geography matter. Do not translate the plan into a ban on all Madrid Airbnb supply.
next_catalyst: Licence issuance, illegal-unit closures, and hotel-pilot conversion economics.

title: Citywide moratorium on new tourist homes
dates: 2025-08-23; maximum three years or earlier planning reform
rule: New tourist-home registrations suspended during planning reform, following earlier restrictions in saturated neighbourhoods. July 2026 follow-up: publication on July 24 of a separate moratorium on new hotels and tourist-apartment blocks on residential land, with pipeline exceptions, further constrains replacement accommodation supply.
observed_evidence: Municipal announcement explains legal basis; dated local reporting confirms commencement.
abnb_implication: Caps the new-host pipeline in a popular destination and shows escalation from neighbourhood to municipal restrictions.
limitations: Existing lawful supply is not automatically removed. Tourist apartments in dedicated buildings and hotels are distinct classifications; gross accommodation supply can still grow.
next_catalyst: PGOU reform, category substitutions and end of suspension.

title: Historic-centre restriction expands to surrounding zones
rule: New STR activities prohibited in zones A1, A3 and A4. Regulation requires five-year authorisations; lawfully operating 2024 units receive a three-year transition under the 2025 framework.
observed_evidence: Current city portal confirms the June expansion was enacted, superseding May 2026 Reuters proposal coverage.
abnb_implication: Expands the geographic reach of housing-driven supply constraints. End of the transition could affect incumbent supply as well as new entry.
limitations: Do not still classify the June expansion as merely proposed. Transitional protection is not an unconditional permanent right; future reductions are not yet quantified.
next_catalyst: Authorisation enforcement, litigation and May 2028 transition end.

title: District-level zero-day STR rule
rule: District sets permitted rental days for covered private/other accommodation to zero; municipal source reports court rejection of the challenge.
observed_evidence: City publication confirms the intended 2026 commencement and planned enforcement using resident reports and platform ads.
abnb_implication: Clear example of resident voting translating into a restrictive local rule; useful policy-diffusion precedent.
limitations: District VI is not all Budapest; accommodation classification matters. Current number of closures and later litigation outcome not independently quantified.
next_catalyst: Enforcement and accommodation reclassification; other district proposals.

title: Law 6/2025 sustainable tourist use of housing
rule: Regional framework ties tourist use of residential housing to planning and a sustainability/housing balance, with transitional arrangements for existing activity.
observed_evidence: Enacted text explicitly links the framework to housing, neighbourhood life and environmental capacity.
abnb_implication: Broadens housing-driven controls beyond individual mainland cities. Local implementation determines practical loss of new or existing supply.
limitations: Not an immediate ban on all holiday rentals. Island-specific and transitional exceptions require granular work; no region-wide revenue haircut inferred.
next_catalyst: Municipal planning, implementing rules and treatment of existing units.

title: STR data-sharing regulation
rule: Regulation (EU) 2024/1028 harmonises registration/data-sharing processes where registration schemes exist, making platform activity more visible to authorities.
observed_evidence: Commission confirms application began May 20, 2026.
abnb_implication: Enforcement infrastructure can make local licence checks more effective and increase platform compliance costs across many markets.
limitations: Not itself an EU-wide night cap or a ban. Avoid counting an EU infrastructure effect and the same local delistings as separate lost bookings.
next_catalyst: Country implementation, data quality and first enforcement actions.

jurisdiction: Spain / communities governed by national Horizontal Property Law
title: Neighbour approval for new tourist letting
rule: New covered tourist rental activity requires express approval by three-fifths of owners representing three-fifths of ownership shares. Qualifying pre-existing lawful activity is grandfathered.
observed_evidence: Official registry decision clarifies that earlier property purchase alone is insufficient for grandfathering.
abnb_implication: Turns neighbour opposition into a property-level barrier to new supply, independently of city quotas.
limitations: Do not automatically apply national condominium provisions to jurisdictions with distinct civil-law regimes, including Catalonia. Tenant opposition is not the same as an owner vote.
next_catalyst: Owner-association votes and litigation over grandfathering.

title: Mandatory STR licences
dates: Existing-host application deadline 2023-10-01; new operators require licence
rule: Mandatory licensing across accommodation types; qualifying existing operators who applied before the deadline can continue pending a decision.
observed_evidence: Current national guidance confirms coverage and transitional operating rights.
abnb_implication: Compliance expense and planning/licensing decisions may constrain urban supply; useful example of neighbourhood-quality regulation.
limitations: A licensing scheme is not itself a national numerical cap. Edinburgh planning control is a separate layer not quantified here.
next_catalyst: Licence refusals, renewals and local planning decisions.

title: STR operating and safety standards
rule: Law 5170/2025 and ministry circular impose accommodation standards including suitable main-use premises, light/ventilation, insurance and safety requirements.
observed_evidence: September 2025 ministry circular sets implementation details ahead of October commencement.
abnb_implication: Can remove unsuitable low-cost inventory or require host spending. Included because adopted in the same policy response to tourism pressure.
limitations: Primarily safety/quality regulation: weaker direct link to gentrification than the district registration freezes. No quantified ABNB impact.
next_catalyst: Inspections and host conversion costs.

title: Illegal-supply enforcement with reported market contraction
rule: Authorities increased scrutiny of unauthorised tourist accommodation alongside broader Spanish restrictions.
observed_evidence: Reuters cites tourism lobby Exceltur: Ibiza short-term tourist supply almost halved year on year in 2025. This is industry data, not Airbnb's own reporting.
abnb_implication: Useful evidence that enforcement can change actual destination inventory, not just create administrative obligations.
limitations: Do not assume the reported supply metric equals unique ABNB listings or revenue. Multi-platform overlap, methodology, broader market forces and policy overlap limit inference.
next_catalyst: Comparable active inventory, booked nights and legal-listing retention.

title: Planned non-renewal of tourist-apartment licences in 2028
rule: City intends not to renew its 10,101 tourist-apartment licences in 2028, using the Catalan licensing framework.
observed_evidence: Official government tourism measure restates the non-renewal objective.
abnb_implication: Potential removal of an established entire-apartment category makes this the highest-priority future local supply cliff.
limitations: 10,101 is a city licence count, not unique ABNB listings or guaranteed lost bookings. Not an already-completed ban. Litigation, implementation and substitute accommodation matter.
next_catalyst: 2028 licence expiry, court proceedings and implementation decisions.

title: Bill 9 apartment-zone vacation-rental phase-out
rule: Removes covered transient vacation-rental use in apartment zoning districts. Mayor separately supports rezoning 4,519 units into new hotel categories.
observed_evidence: County and council confirm passage, signing and revised deadlines.
abnb_implication: Potentially material destination supply reduction after housing activism following the Lahaina disaster. Rezoning can materially reduce the net affected inventory.
limitations: Not a ban on all Maui STRs; do not use older 2028/2030 proposal deadlines. Rezoning recommendations are not proof of completed exemptions.
next_catalyst: Hotel rezoning, lawsuits/stays and final unit-level classification.

title: National STR registration launch
rule: Hosts will need registration with Failte Ireland and display identifiers. Planning compliance is a separate eligibility question.
observed_evidence: Latest government announcement replaces earlier May 2026 launch expectations.
abnb_implication: Could expose non-compliant supply and reduce legal bookability; magnitude depends on planning treatment and enforcement.
limitations: Registration alone does not imply a national STR ban. Commencement/legal implementation should be checked again at launch.
next_catalyst: December launch, final rules and planning guidance.

title: Affordable Housing Act: draft rules for housing-stress areas
rule: Reported draft proposes a framework for assessing housing stress and proportionate local STR restrictions; quantitative caps and grandfathering are among options.
observed_evidence: Reuters obtained a draft; Commission independently confirms work on an Affordable Housing Act. Parliament and member-state consideration still required.
abnb_implication: Highest-priority near-term policy catalyst because a common framework could facilitate restrictions across multiple countries and challenge a city-diversification defence.
limitations: No adopted EU-wide cap. Final text, scope and proportionality protections may differ from the leaked draft.
next_catalyst: September 9 presentation; subsequent Parliament/Council negotiations.

title: Further restrictions on professional multi-property STR operators
status: Municipal policy ambition; passage not established
rule: City proposes limiting tourist letting to main residences and ending permanent multi-property operations.
observed_evidence: Official city statement expresses the desired policy direction.
abnb_implication: Could reach commercial inventory outside the existing occasional-host night cap, increasing impact if enacted.
limitations: Statement of intent is not proof of an operative ban. Legal powers, grandfathering and final text unconfirmed.
next_catalyst: Draft ordinances, enabling law and adoption.

title: Mandatory short-term letting registration
rule: Government guidance says a mandatory national registration scheme is being introduced.
observed_evidence: Current guidance does not establish a completed operational launch in this review.
abnb_implication: Registration may enable local monitoring and future planning restrictions; nationally scalable compliance expense.
limitations: Do not treat a consultation or enabling power as current mandatory registration. Separate from Scotland's live scheme and London's longstanding rules.
next_catalyst: Implementation regulations, launch date and platform obligations.

title: Housing referendum to cancel residential AL registrations
rule: Resident initiative sought cancellation of residential AL registrations and restrictions on new registrations.
observed_evidence: Constitutional Court found the proposed referendum unlawful under the municipal/national legal framework.
abnb_implication: Shows organised local opposition but also a legal constraint on blanket local bans; current risk lies in lawful municipal containment or a redesigned initiative.
limitations: Not a pending approved referendum or an enacted cancellation order. Do not add its hypothetical inventory loss to Lisbon's live restrictions.
next_catalyst: Redesigned referendum or legislation expanding municipal powers.

jurisdiction: Spain / Barcelona, Balearics and other cities
title: Coordinated anti-overtourism protests
status: Activism; linked enacted rules tracked separately
rule: Campaigners challenge housing displacement, tourist saturation and changes to neighbourhood businesses. Water-pistol actions attracted coverage.
observed_evidence: Reuters reported coordinated demonstrations across several Spanish and Italian cities; organisers also planned Lisbon action.
abnb_implication: Political salience and cross-city coordination may sustain tightening even where tourism revenues remain strong.
limitations: No direct ABNB dollar impact attributed to protests. Tourism opposition also targets hotels/cruises; do not treat all activism as anti-STR legislation.
next_catalyst: Concrete bills, electoral commitments and expansion of coalitions.

title: Mass-tourism and housing protests
rule: Demonstrators sought limits on tourism expansion, linking holiday rentals and hotel development to local housing pressure.
observed_evidence: Reuters reported thousands demonstrating in Tenerife.
abnb_implication: Useful chronological link between public pressure and later regional policy attention; supports monitoring islands outside large cities.
limitations: Temporal sequence does not establish protests caused Law 6/2025. No separate supply loss should be assigned to the protest.
next_catalyst: Implementation politics around the regional law and renewed mobilisation.

jurisdiction: Portugal / Lisbon and wider housing movement
title: Housing activism and participation in Southern European mobilisation
status: Activism; specific referendum/legal measures tracked separately
dates: 2023-2025 housing pressure; coordinated mobilisation planned June 2025
rule: Groups link tourism-oriented accommodation to displacement and seek tighter AL restrictions.
observed_evidence: Reuters documented planned Lisbon participation; Constitutional Court record establishes a concrete resident referendum initiative.
abnb_implication: Pressure can persist despite national liberalisation and influence municipal containment decisions.
limitations: Planned protest coverage is not confirmation of attendance or crowd size. Housing activism also concerns wages, construction and other housing policies.
next_catalyst: Municipal elections/decisions, new petitions and enforceable proposals.

title: Resident housing and tourism-capacity pressure
status: Social pressure; no distinct new STR bill established for this row
rule: Public debate concerns worker/student housing, water/energy pressures and neighbourhood displacement in heavily visited destinations.
observed_evidence: AP reports tourism pressure on Greek housing and resources; national and city restrictions are separately documented.
abnb_implication: Signals potential geographic expansion of housing measures; island seasonality may intensify political pressure.
limitations: Weaker activism evidence than Spain: this row records documented social pressure, not a verified nationwide anti-Airbnb protest movement. Cruise/day-visitor measures are not counted as STR bans.
next_catalyst: Specific island/municipal STR proposals and resident campaigns.
